findings.title: Cleanup registers the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP alias
findings.body: `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` uses the literal string "alias" rather than the actual alias (`idp-alias-<i>` / `idp-alias-20`). The 21 identity providers created by testCacheIDPForLogin are therefore never removed (and the cleanup call will fail with 404), leaving leftover IDPs in the realm that can make other tests in the class or run order flaky. Same problem at lines 381 and 425 (and the pre-existing line 303).

findings.title: remove() now always issues a DB lookup by alias
findings.body: Previously `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only executed on the invalidated-cache path; now it is executed unconditionally before deciding, adding an extra database query to every IDP removal even when the entry is cached. It also means the cached-path branch computes `storedIdp` it doesn't use. Consider reusing the cached model for the login-invalidation check.

findings.title: getLoginPredicate can NPE on IDPs with null config
findings.body: The new predicate calls `idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)` whenever `getOrganizationId() != null`. `IdentityProviderModel.getConfig()` is not guaranteed non-null (e.g. models built from partial representations or imports), so a NullPointerException can be thrown from create/update/remove paths that call `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`, breaking the IDP write operation. Use a null-safe access on the config map.

findings.title: getForLogin cache not invalidated/bypassed when the organization changes
findings.body: Unlike `getByOrganization`, which checks `isInvalid(orgId)` in addition to its own cache key, `getForLogin` only checks `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. If an organization is disabled or removed in the same transaction (or its invalidation is registered under the org id), the ORG_ONLY/ALL login lists remain served from cache and still contain the organization's IDPs. Callers that don't re-check `isEnabled()` on the returned wrapped models (only OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean does) will show IDPs of a disabled/removed organization on the login page. Consider also bypassing the cache when `organizationId` is invalidated, and registering login-cache invalidation on organization updates/removal.
